question.text:
Find the solution to the following system of equations.

\[\begin{cases} 2a+3b=-2\\[5pt] \dfrac{a}{3}-\dfrac{b}{6}=-\dfrac{5}{3} \end{cases}\]
question.explanation:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $6.$

\[ \begin{cases} 2a+3b=-2\\[5pt] \dfrac{a}{3}-\dfrac{b}{6}=-\dfrac{5}{3} & \Big| \: \times 6 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} 2a+3b=-2\\[5pt] 2a - b = -10 \end{cases} \]

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $b$ in the second equation:

\begin{align*} 2a - b &= -10 \\[3pt] b &= 2a +10 \end{align*}

Then, we can substitute $b=2a +10$ into the first equation and solve for $a\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2a+3b &= -2 \\[3pt] 2a+3(2a+10) &= -2 \\[3pt] 2a+6a+30 &= -2 \\[3pt] 8a &= -32 \\[3pt] a &= -4 \end{align*}

Finally, to find the value of $b,$ we substitute $a=-4$ into the equation $b=2a+10$ as follows:

\begin{align*} b&=2a+10 \\[3pt] &= 2(-4)+10 \\[3pt] &= -8+10 \\[3pt] &= 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $a=-4, \,b=2.$

example.title: Solving a System Containing Fractions in One Equation Using Substitution

question.text: Find the solution to the following system of equations. \[\begin{cases} x - \dfrac{2}{7}y = 2 \\[3pt] -x + \dfrac{2}{9}y = 2 \end{cases}\]
question.explanation:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $7$ and the second equation by $9,$ as follows:

\[\begin{cases} x -\dfrac{2}{7}y = 2 & \Big| \times 7 \\[5pt] -x + \dfrac{2}{9}y = 2 & \Big| \times 9 \\[5pt] \end{cases} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \begin{cases} 7x - 2y = 14 \\[3pt] -9x + 2y = 18 \end{cases} \]

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. We can eliminate $y$ by adding the two equations: \begin{align} \require{cancel} 7x-\cancel{2y} &= 14\\ -9x+\cancel{2y} &= 18 \\ \hline (7x-9x) &= (14+18) \\[3pt] -2x &= 32 \\[3pt] x &= -16 \end{align}

Finally, we substitute $x=-16$ into the first equation to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 7x - 2y &= 14 \\[3pt] 7(-16) - 2y &= 14 \\[3pt] -112 - 2y &= 14 \\[3pt] -2y &= 126 \\[3pt] y &= -63 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-16$ and $y=-63.$

example.title: Solving a System Containing Fractions in Both Equations Using Elimination

question.text:
Find the solution to the following system of equations:

\[\begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2}x -\dfrac14 y =-1 \\[3pt] \dfrac13 x + \dfrac{1}{2}y = -6 \end{cases}\]
question.explanation:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $6,$ as follows:

\[\begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2}x -\dfrac14 y =-1& \Big| \times 4 \\[5pt] \dfrac13x + \dfrac{1}{2}y = -6& \Big| \times 6 \\ \end{cases} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \begin{cases} 2x -y = -4 \\[3pt] 2x +3y= -36 \end{cases} \]

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-2x$ term that can cancel with the $2x$ term in the second equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 2x -y = -4& \Big| \: \times (-1) \\ 2x +3y= -36& \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} -2x +y = 4 \\ 2x +3y= -36 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $x$-variable, and allows us to solve for $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \cancel{-2x} +y &= 4 \\ \cancel{2x} +3 y &= -36 \\[3pt] \hline (y+3y) &= (4-36)\\[5pt] 4y &= -32 \\[5pt] y &= -\dfrac{32}{4} \\[5pt] y &= -8 \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $y=-8$ into the first equation to solve for $x\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2x -y &= -4 \\[3pt] 2x -(-8) &= -4 \\[3pt] 2x +8 &= -4 \\[3pt] 2x &= -12 \\[3pt] x &= -\dfrac{12}2\\[3pt] x &= -6 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system is $x=-6, \,y=-8.$

example.title: Solving a System Containing Fractions in Both Equations

question.explanation:
To get rid of the fractions in the second equation, we must multiply the second equation by the lowest common denominator of the fractions, which is $3.$ \[ \begin{cases} x - 5y= 7\\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{3}+ 4y=-\dfrac{8}{3} & \Big| \: \times 3 \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} x- 5y= 7\\[3pt] 2x + 12y = -8 \end{cases} \]

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Let's solve for $x$ in the first equation: \begin{align*} x- 5y&=7 \\[3pt] x &= 5y + 7 \end{align*}

Then, we can substitute $x=5y+ 7$ into the second equation and solve for $y\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 2x+ 12y &= -8 \\[5pt] 2(5y+7) + 12y &= -8 \\[5pt] 10y + 14 + 12y &= -8 \\[5pt] 22y + 14 & = -8 \\[5pt] 22y &= -22\\[5pt] y & = -1 \end{align*}

Finally, to find the value of $x,$ we substitute $y=-1$ into the equation $x=5y+7,$ as follows: \begin{align*} x&=5y+ 7 \\[5pt] &= 5(-1) + 7 \\[5pt] &= -5 + 7 \\[5pt] &= 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system of equations is $x=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{2}, \,y=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1}.$

example.title: Solving a System Containing Fractions in One Equation Using Substitution

question.text:
Solve the following system of equations:

\[\begin{cases} \dfrac{5}{4}p + 3q =25\\[5pt] p + \dfrac{2}{5}q = 0 \end{cases}\]
question.explanation:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $4$ and the second equation by $5,$ as follows:

\[\begin{cases} \dfrac{5}{4}p + 3q =25 & \Big| \times 4 \\[5pt] p + \dfrac{2}{5}q = 0& \Big| \times 5 \\ \end{cases} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \begin{cases} 5p + 12q= 100 \\[3pt] 5p + 2q = 0 \end{cases} \]

We will use the elimination method to solve the system. Notice that if we multiply the first equation by $-1,$ then we will get a $-5p$ term that can cancel with the $5p$ term in the second equation:

\[ \begin{cases} 5p + 12q= 100& \Big| \: \times (-1) \\[3pt] 5p + 2q=0& \end{cases} \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad \begin{cases} -5p - 12q = -100 \\[3pt] 5p + 2q = 0 \end{cases} \]

Adding the two equations eliminates the $p$-variable, and allows us to solve for $q\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \cancel{-5p} -12q &=-100 \\[3pt] \cancel{5p} + 2q &= 0 \\[3pt] \hline (-12q +2q ) &= (-100 + 0)\\[5pt] -10q&= -100 \\[5pt] q&= \dfrac{100}{10} \\[5pt] q &= 10 \end{align*}

Finally, we substitute $q=10$ into the second equation to solve for $p\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} 5p +2q &= 0 \\[3pt] 5p + 2\cdot 10 &= 0 \\[3pt] 5p + 20 &= 0 \\[3pt] 5p &= -20 \\[3pt] p &= -4 \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution to the system is $p=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4}, \,q=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}.$
